items.title: 🚨They're not even hiding it anymore.
items.summary:
🚨They're not even hiding it anymore.

A startup called Kled AI just raised $5.5 million to build a "human data marketplace." Backed by the founder of Waymo, Bernard Arnault's venture fund, the owner of the Golden State Warriors, and the founder of MSCHF.

> Their app is already #1 on the app store in 4 countries. Users are uploading 3 to 4.5 million files per day, photos, documents, cloud data, everything. And the top earner is making $7,400 a month selling their data.

Sounds great right? Until you realize what's actually happening.

> They're paying you to hand over the most valuable thing you own, your behavior, your habits, your daily patterns. Then they package it and sell it to AI labs for thousands. You get $7K. They get millions. And the AI that trains on your data is still the thing that replaces you at work next year.

Someone found a way to make humans fund their own replacement and the humans are calling it a side hustle.

But honestly? At least Kled is telling you what's happening to your face. OpenAI scraped your tweets and built a $300 billion company. Meta scraped your photos. Google scraped your code. They all got rich off your data and you got nothing.

> Kled is just the first one honest enough to write you a check while they do it.

The AI was coming for your job whether you sold your data or not. At least now you're getting paid while it learns.

As programming languages evolved, designers needed a safety mechanism. Without one, a single bug — like forgetting a base case — could lock up an entire system. Python's creator, Guido van Rossum, deliberately chose to include a recursion depth limit when he designed Python in the early 1990s. This limit acts as a safety net, stopping runaway recursion before it causes a system crash.

PROBLEM 4— APPLIED [...] Memoization stores the results of previous function calls so they don't need to be computed again. While memoization doesn't directly reduce the maximum recursion depth of a single chain of calls, it can dramatically reduce the number of calls by avoiding redundant computation. For problems like Fibonacci, using `@functools.lru_cache` combined with building up from small values can keep the depth manageable.

These AI-powered tools measure vibrations in surface terrain to determine what lies beneath and how deep structures extend. items.title: WhalesBot Launches Pubbo: AI Companion Robot for US Kids | APG State News | gazettextra.com
items.summary:
SHANGHAI, CN / ACCESS Newswire / November 10, 2026 / WhalesBot, a global leader in AI and educational robotics, today officially announced the launch of Pubbo, an interactive AI companion robot created specifically for American families and children aged 3 to 11. Designed to transform passive screen consumption into active cognitive discovery, Pubbo combines real-time conversational AI, computer vision, generative artwork creation, and interactive STEM learning into an approachable physical [...] Following extensive research and development in child-centric hardware, Pubbo is now available for purchase in the United States through its official platform at pubbo.ai.

Introducing Pubbo: An AI Companion Robot for Kids

Pubbo represents a shift in how children interact with modern technology. Rather than acting as a static teaching device or a repetitive electronic toy, Pubbo is an active, responsive companion that listens, understands, and grows alongside young learners. [...] About WhalesBot

Founded in 2018, WhalesBot is a globally recognized pioneer in robotics, programming tools, and AI learning systems. Driven by the mission to empower the next generation through hands-on technology, WhalesBot bridges hardware innovation, software development, and STEM curriculum into cohesive educational solutions.
